items.title: Understanding Fractional Units
items.explanation: A fractional unit is a part of a whole that results from dividing one whole number into equal parts. Examples include 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, and so on. These units are also called 'unit fractions'.

items.title: Comparing Fractional Units
items.explanation: When dividing a whole into more equal parts, each part becomes smaller. For example, if one roti is shared among 2 children, each gets 1/2 roti. If shared among 4 children, each gets 1/4 roti. Since 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, sharing with more people results in a smaller share.

items.title: Measuring Using Fractional Units
items.explanation: Fractional quantities can be measured by adding fractional units together. For instance, if you have one half (1/2) and add another half (1/2), the total is 2 halves, which equals 1 whole.
